requirements.title: GitHub Client Construction, Lifecycle, and Factory Wiring
requirements.rationale: Direct construction and factory integration allow callers to instantiate authenticated or unauthenticated GitHub adapters configured for public or enterprise instances.

criteria.action: provide a GitHub client adapter struct that implements all methods of the Client interface and export the NewGitHub(Options) (Client, error) constructor
criteria.contract: githubClient implements the issuex.Client interface completely; Authenticated() returns true when holding a non-empty token and false otherwise; Close() closes idle transport connections and returns nil

setup: the issuex package and GitHub client adapter implementation
check.pseudocode:
var _ issuex.Client = (*githubClient)(nil)
c := newTestGitHubClient(Options{Token: "ghp_secret"})
assert c.Authenticated() == true
assert c.Close() == nil

unauth := newTestGitHubClient(Options{})
assert unauth.Authenticated() == false

criteria.condition: NewGitHub is called with Options
criteria.action: resolve BaseURL from Options or GITHUB_API_URL or default to https://api.github.com without trailing slash, Token from Options or GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN, HTTPClient from Options or default 30-second timeout client, and UserAgent from Options or default agent-fox
criteria.contract: BaseURL resolves from Options or GITHUB_API_URL or defaults to https://api.github.com without trailing slash; Token resolves from Options or GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN; default HTTPClient has a 30-second timeout if unspecified; default UserAgent is agent-fox if unspecified

setup: custom Options and process environment variable combinations
check.pseudocode:
c1, _ := NewGitHub(Options{BaseURL: "https://ghe.example.com/api/v3/", Token: "tok1", UserAgent: "custom-ua"})
assert c1.(*githubClient).baseURL == "https://ghe.example.com/api/v3"
assert c1.(*githubClient).token == "tok1"
assert c1.(*githubClient).userAgent == "custom-ua"

t.Setenv("GITHUB_API_URL", "https://api.github.corp/")
t.Setenv("GITHUB_TOKEN", "tok2")
c2, _ := NewGitHub(Options{})
assert c2.(*githubClient).baseURL == "https://api.github.corp"
assert c2.(*githubClient).token == "tok2"
assert c2.(*githubClient).userAgent == "agent-fox"
assert c2.(*githubClient).httpClient.Timeout == 30*time.Second

criteria.condition: NewWithOptions is called with NoOp set to false and the resolved forge type is ForgeTypeGitHub
criteria.action: construct and return the GitHub client adapter instead of returning ErrUnsupportedForge
criteria.contract: NewWithOptions detects ForgeTypeGitHub and returns an active GitHub client adapter rather than ErrUnsupportedForge

setup: Options with remote URL pointing to github.com and NoOp false
check.pseudocode:
client, err := issuex.NewWithOptions(issuex.Options{
    Repo: issuex.Repo{Owner: "agentfox", Name: "agent-fox"},
    RemoteURL: "https://github.com/agentfox/agent-fox.git",
    Token: "dummy-token",
})
assert err == nil
assert client != nil
assert client.Authenticated() == true
assert client.(*githubClient).repo.Owner == "agentfox"

criteria.action: report true from Authenticated() when holding a non-empty token and false otherwise, and close idle HTTP connections on the underlying transport from Close() returning nil

for any outgoing HTTP request, include Accept: application/vnd.github+json, X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28, and User-Agent headers, appending Authorization: Bearer <Token> when authenticated and Content-Type: application/json when a request body is present
criteria.contract: Accept header is always application/vnd.github+json; X-GitHub-Api-Version is always 2022-11-28; User-Agent is always populated; Authorization header contains Bearer token when authenticated and is omitted when unauthenticated; Content-Type is application/json when request body is present

requirements.title: Repository Metadata and Merge Policy Inspection
requirements.rationale: Repository inspection verifies repository accessibility, permissions, default branch, and allowed merge strategies for pull request automation.

criteria.condition: GetRepository is called with a valid Repo
criteria.action: execute GET /repos/{owner}/{name} and populate a Repository struct with FullName, DefaultBranch, Private, Archived, and Permissions booleans for Push, Pull, and Admin
criteria.contract: FullName, DefaultBranch, Private, Archived, and Permissions booleans are accurately populated; merge strategy flags allow_merge_commit, allow_squash_merge, and allow_rebase_merge are recorded in the client

setup: a mock server returning GitHub repository JSON with permissions and merge strategy flags
check.pseudocode:
srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    assert r.Method == "GET"
    assert r.URL.Path == "/repos/owner/test-repo"
    w.Write([]byte(`{
        "full_name": "owner/test-repo",
        "default_branch": "main",
        "private": true,
        "archived": false,
        "permissions": {"push": true, "pull": true, "admin": false},
        "allow_merge_commit": true,
        "allow_squash_merge": false,
        "allow_rebase_merge": true
    }`))
}))
defer srv.Close()
c := newTestGitHubClient(Options{BaseURL: srv.URL, Token: "tok"})
repo, err := c.GetRepository(context.Background(), Repo{Owner: "owner", Name: "test-repo"})
assert err == nil
assert repo.FullName == "owner/test-repo"
assert repo.DefaultBranch == "main"
assert repo.Private == true
assert repo.Archived == false
assert repo.Permissions.Push == true && repo.Permissions.Pull == true && repo.Permissions.Admin == false
assert c.allowMergeCommit == true && c.allowSquashMerge == false && c.allowRebaseMerge == true

criteria.condition: GetRepository receives a successful repository response
criteria.action: record the repository merge strategy booleans allow_merge_commit, allow_squash_merge, and allow_rebase_merge for pull request merge method resolution

requirements.title: Issue Lifecycle and Retrieval
requirements.rationale: Issue lifecycle methods enable creating, reading with full comment history, updating, closing, and filtered listing of forge issues.

criteria.condition: CreateIssue is called with a Repo and CreateIssueRequest on an authenticated client
criteria.action: execute POST /repos/{owner}/{name}/issues with title, body, and labels, returning the created Issue with Number, Title, Body, State, URL, Author, Labels, timestamps, and IsPR set to false
criteria.contract: POST request is sent to /repos/{owner}/{name}/issues with title, body, and labels; returned Issue struct has Number, Title, Body, State, URL, Author, Labels, and IsPR set to false

setup: an authenticated GitHub client and mock server handling POST /repos/{owner}/{name}/issues
check.pseudocode:
srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    assert r.Method == "POST"
    assert r.URL.Path == "/repos/owner/repo/issues"
    var body map[string]any
    json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&body)
    assert body["title"] == "Bug title"
    assert body["body"] == "Bug body"
    assert body["labels"].([]any)[0] == "bug"
    w.WriteHeader(http.StatusCreated)
    w.Write([]byte(`{
        "number": 12,
        "title": "Bug title",
        "body": "Bug body",
        "state": "open",
        "html_url": "https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/12",
        "user": {"login": "alice"},
        "labels": [{"name": "bug"}],
        "created_at": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "updated_at": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    }`))
}))
defer srv.Close()
c := newTestGitHubClient(Options{BaseURL: srv.URL, Token: "tok"})
issue, err := c.CreateIssue(context.Background(), Repo{Owner: "owner", Name: "repo"}, CreateIssueRequest{
    Title: "Bug title", Body: "Bug body", Labels: []string{"bug"},
})
assert err == nil
assert issue.Number == 12
assert issue.Title == "Bug title"
assert issue.Author.Login == "alice"
assert issue.Labels[0].Name == "bug"
assert issue.IsPR == false

criteria.contract: returns an error satisfying IsNoToken(err) == true

setup: an authenticated GitHub client and mock server handling issue PATCH and comment POST
check.pseudocode:
var calls []string
srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    calls = append(calls, r.Method+" "+r.URL.Path)
    if r.Method == "POST" && strings.HasSuffix(r.URL.Path, "/comments") {
        w.WriteHeader(http.StatusCreated)
        w.Write([]byte(`{"html_url": "https://cmt/1"}`))
        return
    }
    if r.Method == "PATCH" {
        var body map[string]any
        json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&body)
        w.Write([]byte(fmt.Sprintf(`{"number": 5, "title": "%s", "state": "%s"}`, body["title"], body["state"])))
        return
    }
}))
defer srv.Close()
c := newTestGitHubClient(Options{BaseURL: srv.URL, Token: "tok"})
ctx := context.Background()
ref := IssueRef{Repo: Repo{Owner: "o", Name: "r"}, Number: 5}

upd, errUpd := c.UpdateIssue(ctx, ref, UpdateIssueRequest{Title: "New Title"})
assert errUpd == nil
assert upd.Title == "New Title"

errClose := c.CloseIssue(ctx, ref, "Closing as completed")
assert errClose == nil
assert calls[1] == "POST /repos/o/r/issues/5/comments"
assert calls[2] == "PATCH /repos/o/r/issues/5"

requirements.title: Issue Comments and Label Operations
requirements.rationale: Comments and labels provide issue interaction and triage categorization with idempotent mutation semantics.

criteria.condition: AddComment is called with an IssueRef and comment body on an authenticated client
criteria.action: execute POST /repos/{owner}/{name}/issues/{number}/comments with the comment body and return the comment html_url
criteria.contract: AddComment executes POST to /comments with body and returns comment html_url; ListComments paginates up to 5 pages (500 comments) and sets CommentList.Truncated to true when page 5 contains 100 items

setup: an authenticated GitHub client and mock server handling issue comments
check.pseudocode:
srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    if r.Method == "POST" {
        var body map[string]string
        json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&body)
        assert body["body"] == "test comment"
        w.WriteHeader(http.StatusCreated)
        w.Write([]byte(`{"html_url": "https://github.com/o/r/issues/1#issuecomment-1"}`))
        return
    }
    page := r.URL.Query().Get("page")
    if page == "5" {
        // Return 100 items on 5th page to trigger truncation
        w.Write(makeCommentPageJSON(100))
        return
    }
    w.Write(makeCommentPageJSON(100))
}))
defer srv.Close()
c := newTestGitHubClient(Options{BaseURL: srv.URL, Token: "tok"})

url, err := c.AddComment(context.Background(), ref, "test comment")

cmts, errList := c.ListComments(context.Background(), ref)
assert errList == nil

requirements.title: Pull Request Checks, Reviews, and Merge Execution
requirements.rationale: CI status checks, review commenting, and policy-aware pull request merging enable complete automation of review and integration pipelines.

criteria.condition: GetCIChecks is called with an IssueRef
criteria.action: resolve the pull request head commit SHA via ReadPullRequest and execute GET /repos/{owner}/{name}/commits/{head_sha}/check-runs, returning mapped CheckRun structs
criteria.contract: GetCIChecks resolves PR head SHA via ReadPullRequest and queries /commits/{head_sha}/check-runs; GetPRReviews normalizes review states to lowercase approved, changes_requested, commented, or dismissed; PostReviewComment executes POST /reviews with event COMMENT and body

setup: an authenticated GitHub client and mock server handling commit check runs, reviews, and review comments
check.pseudocode:
srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    if r.URL.Path == "/repos/o/r/pulls/7" && r.Method == "GET" {
        w.Write([]byte(`{"number": 7, "head": {"sha": "commit_sha_123"}}`))
        return
    }
    if r.URL.Path == "/repos/o/r/commits/commit_sha_123/check-runs" {
        w.Write([]byte(`{"check_runs": [{"name": "ci/test", "status": "completed", "conclusion": "success", "output": {"summary": "Passed"}, "html_url": "https://ci/1"}]}`))
        return
    }
    if r.URL.Path == "/repos/o/r/pulls/7/reviews" && r.Method == "GET" {
        w.Write([]byte(`[{"user": {"login": "eve"}, "state": "CHANGES_REQUESTED", "body": "Needs fixes", "submitted_at": "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"}]`))
        return
    }
    if r.URL.Path == "/repos/o/r/pulls/7/reviews" && r.Method == "POST" {
        var body map[string]any
        json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&body)
        assert body["event"] == "COMMENT"
        assert body["body"] == "Looks promising"
        w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
        w.Write([]byte(`{}`))
        return
    }
}))
defer srv.Close()
c := newTestGitHubClient(Options{BaseURL: srv.URL, Token: "tok"})
ref := IssueRef{Repo: Repo{Owner: "o", Name: "r"}, Number: 7}

checks, errChecks := c.GetCIChecks(context.Background(), ref)
assert errChecks == nil
assert len(checks) == 1
assert checks[0].Name == "ci/test"
assert checks[0].Conclusion == "success"

reviews, errReviews := c.GetPRReviews(context.Background(), ref)
assert errReviews == nil
assert len(reviews) == 1
assert reviews[0].State == "changes_requested" // normalized to lowercase

errComment := c.PostReviewComment(context.Background(), ref, "Looks promising")
assert errComment == nil

requirements.title: GitHub REST Transport, Error Handling, and Rate Limiting
requirements.rationale: Bounded memory usage, rate-limit backoff with retry, and canonical error classification ensure resilience against GitHub API failures and throttling.

criteria.action: read all HTTP response bodies through an io.LimitReader bounded to at most 8 MB (8388608 bytes)
criteria.contract: response reader is bounded to at most 8,388,608 bytes via io.LimitReader preventing unbounded memory growth

setup: a mock server generating an HTTP response body exceeding 8 MB

criteria.condition: an HTTP response has status 429 or status 403 with header X-RateLimit-Remaining 0 and the calculated RetryAfter backoff duration is less than or equal to 120 seconds
criteria.action: invoke the configured sleep function for the backoff duration and retry the request once
criteria.contract: the custom sleep function is invoked for the backoff duration and the request is retried once when backoff <= 120 seconds; returns an error satisfying IsRateLimited(err) == true when backoff > 120 seconds or retry fails; the injected sleep function is called instead of time.Sleep during retries

setup: a GitHub client configured with an injected sleep function and mock server simulating 429 and 403 quota exhaustion
check.pseudocode:
var slept time.Duration
sleepFn := func(d time.Duration) { slept = d }

// Case 1: 429 with 5-second backoff succeeds on retry
attempts := 0
srv1 := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    attempts++
    if attempts == 1 {
        w.Header().Set("Retry-After", "5")
        w.WriteHeader(http.StatusTooManyRequests)
        return
    }
    w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
    w.Write([]byte(`{"full_name": "o/r"}`))
}))
defer srv1.Close()
c1 := newTestGitHubClient(Options{BaseURL: srv1.URL, Token: "tok"})
c1.sleep = sleepFn
_, err1 := c1.GetRepository(context.Background(), Repo{Owner: "o", Name: "r"})
assert err1 == nil
assert attempts == 2
assert slept == 5*time.Second

// Case 2: 403 quota exhaustion with > 120s backoff aborts immediately
srv2 := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    w.Header().Set("X-RateLimit-Remaining", "0")
    w.Header().Set("X-RateLimit-Reset", strconv.FormatInt(time.Now().Add(200*time.Second).Unix(), 10))
    w.WriteHeader(http.StatusForbidden)
}))
defer srv2.Close()
c2 := newTestGitHubClient(Options{BaseURL: srv2.URL, Token: "tok"})
c2.sleep = sleepFn
_, err2 := c2.GetRepository(context.Background(), Repo{Owner: "o", Name: "r"})
assert issuex.IsRateLimited(err2) == true

criteria.condition: an HTTP response has status 429 or status 403 with header X-RateLimit-Remaining 0 and the RetryAfter backoff exceeds 120 seconds, or a retried rate-limited request fails
criteria.action: abort the request and return an error wrapping ErrRateLimited
criteria.contract: returns an error satisfying IsRateLimited(err) == true

criteria.condition: an HTTP response returns status 404, 409, or 405
criteria.action: wrap the corresponding sentinel error ErrNotFound for status 404 or ErrConflict for status 409 and 405 in the returned HTTPError
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 response wraps ErrNotFound in the returned HTTPError; HTTP 409 and 405 responses wrap ErrConflict in the returned HTTPError

setup: a mock server returning HTTP 404, 409, and 405 error responses
check.pseudocode:
srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    switch r.URL.Path {
    case "/404":
        w.WriteHeader(http.StatusNotFound)
        w.Write([]byte(`{"message": "Not Found"}`))
    case "/409":
        w.WriteHeader(http.StatusConflict)
        w.Write([]byte(`{"message": "Conflict"}`))
    case "/405":
        w.WriteHeader(http.StatusMethodNotAllowed)
        w.Write([]byte(`{"message": "Method Not Allowed"}`))
    }
}))
defer srv.Close()
c := newTestGitHubClient(Options{BaseURL: srv.URL, Token: "tok"})

err404 := c.do(context.Background(), "GET", "/404", nil, nil)
assert issuex.IsNotFound(err404) == true
assert errors.Is(err404, issuex.ErrNotFound)

err409 := c.do(context.Background(), "POST", "/409", nil, nil)
assert issuex.IsConflict(err409) == true
assert errors.Is(err409, issuex.ErrConflict)

err405 := c.do(context.Background(), "PUT", "/405", nil, nil)
assert issuex.IsConflict(err405) == true
assert errors.Is(err405, issuex.ErrConflict)

execution_paths.title: Rate-limit backoff and retry recovery on GitHub REST request

steps.action: calls GetRepository on an authenticated GitHub client
executes GET /repos/{owner}/{name} and receives an HTTP 403 response with X-RateLimit-Remaining 0 and Retry-After header of 2 seconds
calculates the backoff duration via RetryAfter() and invokes the injected sleep function for the duration
retries the GET /repos/{owner}/{name} request once
receives HTTP 200 and returns the populated Repository struct to the caller

setup: an authenticated GitHub client with an injected zero-delay sleep function and mock server simulating 403 quota exhaustion on first attempt
